source.title: QDrop: Randomly Dropping Quantization for Extremely Low-bit Post-Training Quantization
source.authors: Xiuying Wei; Ruihao Gong; Yuhang Li; Xiang-Long Liu; Feng-Wei Yu

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares flatness measures and train/test accuracy across PTQ settings, bearing on whether measured flatness tracks the generalization gap, but does not use the specific generalization-measure comparison in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper studies post-training quantization, not memorization of arbitrary labels or standard training on natural labels. Its ImageNet quantization accuracy comparisons and other task results do not test the listed versions. Rows below cover the ResNet-18 comparisons of flatness and train/test accuracy that bear on V7; comparisons between PTQ methods are otherwise omitted.
record.test_reason: The study uses flatness to motivate and evaluate a post-training quantization method. It does not test V7's ranking of generalization gaps among networks with similarly low training loss: the accuracy gaps are reported for W2A2, Hessian measurements for W3A3, and Figure 2 compares calibration versus test sharpness rather than sharpness versus generalization gaps. Its remaining experiments test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that incorporating activation quantization and randomly dropping portions during reconstruction promotes flatter quantized models and improves held-out accuracy. They identify greater calibration-set overfitting in Case 2 than Case 3.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines post-training quantization reconstruction and quantization-induced flatness, rather than the generalization-measure comparison described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The reconstruction case (Cases 1–3 versus QDrop) changes sharpness and the train/test accuracy gap; the paper also reports that QDrop probability affects ImageNet accuracy and that 0.5 generally performs best among the tested candidates.

fits_no_version.finding: W2A2 reconstruction settings produce calibration/test accuracy gaps of 0.94, 23.77, 21.85 and 14.97 percentage points for Case 1, Case 2, Case 3 and QDrop respectively; Case 1 performs poorly on both datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PTQ reconstruction choices affect calibration-set overfitting and held-out quantization accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-aware reconstruction improves calibration-data flatness; QDrop has the lowest reported W3A3 Hessian statistics and a smoother illustrated test loss landscape.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Introducing and randomly dropping activation quantization can improve flatness and accuracy in low-bit PTQ.

record.problems: The direct train/test comparison is reported for one model and one quantization setting. Sharpness comparisons in Figure 2 are figure-only, and the Hessian metrics are indirect measures of flatness rather than the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.
record.rows_left_out: ImageNet classification, object detection, NLP, and calibration-size or cross-domain results compare quantization performance but do not measure the generalization gap or a property named by a claim version. Other quantization-method comparisons in Tables 2–6 are therefore not included.

untested.parts: Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Conventional dropout effects on held-out error. Dropping activation quantization is a different intervention.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical discussion explicitly considers perturbations scaled to parameter magnitude. The exclusion from V7 rests on the empirical target and unmatched measurements, not simply on a different dataset or the absence of magnitude-aware reasoning.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under standard training.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
The paper does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures or test the stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN setting.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 W2A2
rows.operation_detail: PTQ reconstruction with Case 1, keeping activations full precision during reconstruction
rows.note: The paper reports paired train and test accuracy; this low test accuracy is the Case 1 reference for the other settings.
rows.check: Table 8 accurately reports test accuracy 18.88%, with calibration accuracy 19.82%. This method comparator does not measure V7; its small 0.94-point gap accompanies poor accuracy on both datasets.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 W2A2
rows.operation_detail: PTQ reconstruction with Case 2, introducing activation quantization during weight tuning
rows.note: Case 2 has a large calibration/test difference: train accuracy 69.54 and test accuracy 45.77.
rows.check: Table 8 reports test accuracy 45.77% and calibration accuracy 69.54%, a 23.77-point gap. These are PTQ calibration results, without a corresponding magnitude-aware sharpness measurement establishing V7.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 W2A2
rows.operation_detail: PTQ reconstruction with Case 3, omitting activation quantization inside the current tuning block
rows.note: Case 3 has train accuracy 69.92 and test accuracy 48.07.
rows.check: Values are correct; calibration accuracy is 69.92%, giving a 21.85-point gap. This comparison measures reconstruction-method overfitting, without a matched V7 sharpness-versus-gap evaluation.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 W2A2
rows.operation_detail: PTQ reconstruction with QDrop, randomly dropping activation quantization
rows.note: QDrop has train accuracy 66.11 and test accuracy 51.14, a smaller train/test difference than Case 2 or Case 3.
rows.check: Values are correct; calibration accuracy is 66.11%, giving a 14.97-point gap. QDrop's improved test performance and smaller calibration gap do not establish V7's relation under similarly low training loss.

reader_labels.reason: Train/test accuracy and the reported flatness comparisons vary across reconstruction settings: Case 2 has a much larger train/test difference than Case 3 or QDrop, while the paper's sharpness and Hessian results are not the specific magnitude-aware measure in V7 (R1–R10).
